- Hubs: each degree ≥ 14 ⟹ 2x + y ≥ 5·14 = 70.
- Outposts: each degree ≤ 3 ⟹ y + 2z ≤ 19·3 = 57.

---

## Part M: maximum outpost–outpost edges

Since x ≤ C(5,2) = 10, the hub constraint gives y ≥ 70 − 2x ≥ 70 − 20 = **50**.  
Then the outpost constraint gives 2z ≤ 57 − y ≤ 57 − 50 = 7, so **z ≤ 3**.

| 1 | 10 | 19 ✓ |
| 2 | 20 | 38 ✓ |
| 3 | 30 | 50 ✓ |
| 4 | 40 | 50 ✓ |
| 5 | 50 | 50 ✓ |

So the bipartite graph exists, hence **M = 3**. (z = 4 would force y ≤ 49 < 50, impossible.)

## Part K: minimum islands with no research hub

Five hubs can occupy at most 5 distinct islands, so at least 9 − 5 = **4** islands have no hub. This is attainable (place one hub per island on 5 islands; degree ≥ 14 is satisfiable since each hub can connect to all 4 other hubs + 10 of 19 outposts). Therefore **K = 4**.

---

## Part E: minimum guaranteed islands with zero internal edges

E = min over all valid configurations of (number of islands with no internal ferry route).

**Upper bound on E (constructing a config with only 1 empty island).** Place hubs h₁,…,h₅ on islands I₁,…,I₅, each with one outpost o₁,…,o₅, giving internal hub–outpost edges hᵢ–oᵢ. Place outpost pairs on I₆, I₇, I₈ with internal outpost–outpost edges (o₆–o₇, o₈–o₉, o₁₀–o₁₁). Place the remaining 8 outposts on I₉ with **no** internal edges.

Use the degree structure from Part M: complete hub graph (x=10), 3 outpost–outpost edges (z=3), y=50 hub–outpost edges. The 6 outposts on I₆–I₈ have outpost-degree 1, so they need hub-degree 2 (total 3). The 5 outposts o₁–o₅ have outpost-degree 0, need hub-degree 3 (one needs 2). The 8 outposts on I₉ need hub-degree 3 (or 2 for the degree-2 one).

After fixing the 5 internal hub–outpost edges, the residual bipartite sequence is: hubs [9,9,9,9,9], outposts [3×8, 2×10, 1×1] (sum 45 = 45). Gale–Ryser checks:

| k | Σrᵢ | Σmin(cⱼ,k) |

| 2 | 18 | 37 ✓ |
| 3 | 27 | 45 ✓ |
| 4 | 36 | 45 ✓ |

All pass, so the configuration exists with exactly **1** island (I₉) having no internal edge.

**Lower bound on E (no config achieves 0).** With 5 hubs, at most 5 islands contain a hub, so **at least 4 islands have no hub**. An island with no hub contains only outposts, so any internal edge there must be an outpost–outpost edge. But z ≤ 3 in every valid configuration (proved in Part M). Therefore at most 3 of the ≥4 hub-free islands can have an internal edge, forcing **at least 1** island to have no internal edge.

Combining: **E = 1**.

---

$$M + K + E = 3 + 4 + 1 = \boxed{8}$$
